question: Assume today is 2026-04-18. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate China's total retail sales of consumer goods (社会消费品零售总额) for the single month of April 2026 (not the January-April cumulative total), in Chinese yuan (CNY; the release states it in 亿元, i.e. units of 100 million yuan), as it will be first reported in the National Bureau of Statistics of China's monthly release on retail sales of consumer goods.

target.what: Single-month total retail sales of consumer goods (社会消费品零售总额) in mainland China, covering retail sales of goods and catering services to consumers, as first reported by NBS for April 2026; excludes services retail sales outside goods/catering and excludes Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan.
target.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS)
target.cadence: Monthly; April single-month value is first reported in the May monthly release, typically mid-May, together with the January-April cumulative total.
target.caveats: At the 2026-04-18 cutoff, April 2026 is not yet complete (ongoing/future), so this is a forecast of the first reported value, which is preliminary and subject to revision. NBS retail sales covers goods retail and catering revenue, not total household consumption expenditure or broader services retai

candidates.perspective: NBS monthly statistical releases and historical time series
candidates.hypothesis: April 2026 retail sales can be bridged from recent NBS monthly history using April/March seasonal ratios or April-vs-Q1 patterns; recent 2026 momentum (January-February and March, if released by cutoff) constrains the year-on-year growth rate applied to the April 2025 level.
candidates.data_to_find: NBS monthly total retail sales in 亿元 for April 2023, April 2024, April 2025; March 2025 and March 2026; January-February 2026; Q1 2026 if available; monthly year-on-year growth rates; April/March seasonal ratio and April share of Q2 in prior years. Minimum evidence: April 2025 level, March 2026 level, and Q1 2026 growth.

Minimum evidence: category weights and an early-April auto signal.

This is a dimensionless change factor applied to the observed March level, not an assumed target level.
assumptions.applies_when: April 2026 has no nationwide mobility restriction, major statistical break, or extreme holiday-timing shift relative to normal years.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that April 2026 retail sales are at or above March 2026, or historical April/March ratios consistently outside the stated range.

assumptions.applies_when: The April 2026 monthly seasonal pattern is broadly normal and the Q1 2026 total is not materially revised before the April release.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that April's share of Q1 is persistently outside the stated range in 2026 due to policy timing or a statistical break.

assumptions.rationale: March has 31 days and April 30, and April normally lacks a major e-commerce festival while still having Qingming and spring demand. I use 66 CNY/parcel as a central conversion, with a range for mix shifts between low-value and high-value parcels.

assumptions.name: April 2026 online goods share relative to Q1 2026 online goods share
assumptions.rationale: p5 gives a Q1 2026 online-goods share of 24.8%. April online share is usually higher than the Q1 average because Q1 includes the Jan-Feb holiday period with more offline spending. A modest upward adjustment of about 10% is consistent with historical April-versus-Q1 patterns; the range keeps the share in roughly 25.8%-28.8%.
assumptions.applies_when: Used in m1 to adjust p5 Q1 online share to an April share; if April online share were exactly the Q1 share, this ratio would be 1.0.

assumptions.applies_when: Used in m2 to convert p21 cumulative trade-in sales through Apr 10 into an April full-month trade-in sales estimate; it assumes the daily trade-in pace does not shift drastically after Apr 10.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that April trade-in sales were far below 25% or far above 36% of the Jan 1-Apr 10 cumulative total, such as a sudden program suspension or a large late-April surge.

assumptions.name: Consumer goods trade-in sales share of total retail sales in April 2026

assumptions.applies_when: Used in m2 to scale trade-in sales up to total retail sales; it assumes the April trade-in sales share is near the early-2026 ratio and that trade-in sales remain within NBS goods retail coverage.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that trade-in sales were below 2.8% or above 3.9% of April total retail sales, or that a large part of trade-in sales fell outside the NBS retail definition.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
